about.title: Sunnyvale Product Liability Claims
about.longDescription: Sunnyvale sits in the heart of Santa Clara County's technology corridor, so it is no surprise that many of the products people use here were designed, tested, or sold within a few miles of home. When one of those products fails — a battery that overheats, a power tool with a guard that slips, a child seat that does not latch the way the label says — the injury can be serious even when the user did everything right. California treats these cases differently from most other injury claims. Under strict liability, you usually do not have to prove the manufacturer was careless. You show that the product had a design, manufacturing, or warning defect and that the defect caused your harm. Vehicle components matter here too: of the 457 injury collisions in Sunnyvale in 2025, some may involve equipment questions like airbag timing or tire failure that deserve a closer look. LawProactive is a free service, not a law firm. We connect Sunnyvale residents with an independent attorney who handles product cases on contingency.

whyChoose.title: Why Sunnyvale Residents Use LawProactive for Product Claims

items.title: Strict Liability Changes the Question
items.desc: In California you generally do not need to prove the maker was negligent — only that the product was defective in its design, manufacturing, or warnings and that the defect caused your injury. The attorneys we connect you with build cases around that standard.

items.title: Every Link in the Chain Can Be Responsible
items.desc: The manufacturer, the distributor, and the store on El Camino Real that sold the product may each be liable under California law. An attorney can identify who belongs in the claim rather than letting one party point at another.

items.title: The Product Is the Evidence
items.desc: Keeping the failed item, its packaging, and any receipts is often the difference between a provable case and a guess. Our network attorneys can tell you early what to preserve and how.

items.question: My airbag never deployed in a crash on SR-237. Is that a product liability case or just a car accident case?
items.answer: It can be both. The other driver may be responsible for the collision itself, while the vehicle or airbag maker may be responsible for a component that did not perform as designed. An attorney will usually want the vehicle preserved before it is repaired or scrapped, so speak with someone before signing anything with your insurer or a salvage yard.

items.question: Do I have to prove the company knew the product was defective?
items.answer: Generally, no. California product liability often operates under strict liability, which means the focus is on whether the product had a design, manufacturing, or warning defect and whether that defect caused your injury. Whether the company knew or acted carelessly is usually not something you need to establish.

items.question: I threw away the broken product after I was hurt. Do I still have a claim?
items.answer: Possibly, but it is harder, so do not throw away anything else. Photos, the box, the receipt, the model number, and any medical records that describe the injury can all help. An attorney in our network can review what you still have and tell you honestly whether the case can move forward; LawProactive does not charge for that connection.
